prompt.brief: Design a polite, distributed web crawler that discovers and fetches billions of pages, respects robots and host limits, avoids duplicates and traps, and produces replayable crawl data.
successSignals: Define URL canonicalization, discovery, fetch, redirect, robots, politeness, content identity, revisit, and durable frontier semantics.
Partition by host for per-domain concurrency/rate limits, deduplicate globally, and prevent infinite loops, traps, oversized content, and unbounded queues.
Separate frontier scheduling from fetch workers, parsing, storage, and indexing; make leases, retries, checkpoints, and replay explicit.
Explain abuse handling, takedown/privacy, TLS failures, poisoned pages, observability, bandwidth cost, and graceful slowdown.

functional: Seed and discover URLs, canonicalize and prioritize them, fetch politely, parse links/content, store responses, and emit crawl metadata.
Support robots.txt/HTTP policies, redirects, retries, conditional requests, content hashing, revisit schedules, and host-level dashboards.
Provide pause/resume, URL/domain exclusion, deletion/takedown, checkpoint recovery, and deterministic replay of frontier decisions.
nonFunctional: Guarantee bounded per-host concurrency and a crawl decision within seconds while preventing unbounded retries or spider traps.
Scale to billions of pages and millions of hosts without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 10B pages, 10M hosts, and 1M fetches per second peak
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Polite, distributed web crawler commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Polite, distributed web crawler writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Polite, distributed web crawler version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Polite, distributed web crawler by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Polite, distributed web crawler work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Polite, distributed web crawler projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Polite, distributed web crawler projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Polite, distributed web crawler records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Polite, distributed web crawler latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
